children.author: miohtama
children.text:
It sounded like a good deal?

> The marketplace sellers that we caught only had to list a model at the lowest price, enable request logging, and wait. What stood out is how personal it was – these were individuals, working from what looked like home internet connections and personal computers, trying to break into our canary servers one login at a time.

> In one case, we sent two prompts through a single seller’s offer. About a day and a half later, someone on a home broadband connection opened both secret URLs in a desktop browser and started guessing usernames at the login page. Prompts for the same model that went through a different seller were never touched, which tells us that the leak follows the seller and not the marketplace as a whole.

children.author: qbatten
children.text:
So insane.

My takeaway is: Only use hyperscalers or major first party vendors (like the "labs").

If using routers or marketplaces, assume anything that goes in is public
